91c14665-8b06-47a9-9c56-03d5eef496c9.title: ‘White-hot fury’: Hawks rage over forgotten ump call as big rule change revealed
91c14665-8b06-47a9-9c56-03d5eef496c9.incipit: An angry Sam Mitchell reacted with “white-hot fury” to a series of crucial umpire decisions in the dying moments of Hawthorn’s heartbreaking preliminary final loss to Brisbane, as debate continues to rage...
91c14665-8b06-47a9-9c56-03d5eef496c9.body: An angry Sam Mitchell reacted with “white-hot fury” to a series of crucial umpire decisions in the dying moments of Hawthorn’s heartbreaking preliminary final loss to Brisbane , as debate continues to rage around the footy world. Hawks fans were left incensed at the MCG when three decisions in a row went against them in the final minute, leading to Hugh McCluggage’s match-winning goal. The most infamous has clearly been the call by umpire Hayden Meyer to penalise Jarman Impey for holding the ball , with the Hawk ruled to have not made a genuine attempt to dispose of the football. That decision, which set up McCluggage’s go-ahead major, was declared “100 per cent right” by Fox Footy commentator Gerard Whateley. But post-match, Mitchell declared that free was “probably not the one I was focused on”, with the Hawks coach reacting furiously in the box as a Grand Final spot was wrested from his team’s grasp. “A couple leading up to it and other key moments in the game,” he said of the incidents that had frustrated him most. “I’m sure the umpires will assess how they performed in the game in key moments. “The Mitch Lewis out of bounds one and the (Dayne) Zorko free kick. “It’s not for me to say.” More coverage... ‘NOT GOING TO SLEEP WELL’: Star lashes out at ump call ‘DEEPEST OF PAIN’: Rawest presser you’ll see ‘DON’T DO THAT’: Fans called out over ump act HAWKS RATINGS: Perfect score for ‘twilight robbery’ LIONS RATINGS: ‘Coldest to hottest’ in fantasy quarter "The biggest call you have ever seen!" | 00:41 A minute earlier, key forward Lewis, tracking down a bouncing ball down the Shane Warne Stand wing from Jack Ginnivan, had the ball bounce off his fingers and over the boundary line. Hawks fans exploded in outrage when the free kick was paid against him for insufficient intent. Then, moments later, Josh Weddle was penalised for high contact after clipping Dayne Zorko as the Lion skirted around an attempted tackle. Replays showed the Hawk had made glancing, but far from severe, contact with Zorko’s head. “That was white-hot fury from Sam there, who let’s face it, was really strong,” Fox Footy reporter Jon Ralph said of Mitchell’s press conference. Mitch Lewis was penalised for insufficient intent. Source: FOX SPORTS Harris Andrews successfully appealed for the free kick. Source: FOX SPORTS “Basically said “I’m sure the umpires will assess how they performed in the game in those key moments.” Of the Lewis incident, Ralph declared the umpire had made the “correct call”, citing a contentious mid-season rule change that prevented players from circumventing the introduced “last disposal” rule by getting a touch to the ball as it crossed the line. The tweak has caused controversy throughout the season, with a call to penalise Carlton defender Nick Haynes for insufficient intent in the Blues’ Gather Round loss to Adelaide copping a particularly savage backlash. “You have to try and drag the ball in,” Ralph said. “It is the correct call – you remember down in Geelong, we had a couple of incidents like that about Round 6, and we saw the rules change mid-season.” Josh Weddle conceded a high free kick against Dayne Zorko. Source: FOX SPORTS Ralph added on X: “It’s no consolation for Hawthorn but until round 3 Mitch Lewis could take the ball over the line like that in the last 90 seconds.” “Then players were diving for the line just to get a fingernail on the ball to avoid a lasso free kick,” he wrote. “So the AFL changed the rule mid-season to ensure a player had to attempt to bring the ball back in rather than escorting it out. “Unfortunately for the Hawks it reared its head in the dying seconds.” However, a trio of former greats in Jordan Lewis, Tom Hawkins and Jonathan Brown disagreed with Ralph, saying Lewis was “stiff” to have been pinged. “That’s for me the wrong call,” Hawks four-time premiership great Lewis said on Fox Footy “I’m not too sure what you’re meant to do there when you’re going full speed towards the boundary line. “The ball was bouncing that way. “I just thought that was a big call to make in a really important part of the game. “I think what they’re asking players to do is to somehow get a hand behind the ball. It’s pretty hard when you’re out, fully stretched, to try and (do that).” “What if he took possession of that and fell over (the boundary line)?” Lions champion Brown wondered. Bottles thrown at umpires post match | 01:21 “Do you think it would have been still paid?”. “I don’t think it’s deliberate,” Lewis replied. “I actually think he’s trying to take possession,” Hawkins added. “That’s probably the nuances in it, but for me, that was an important part of the game,” Lewis finished. “It seemed like a 50/50, I know the AFL will probably come out and tick that one off, but that was free kick, bang-bang-bang, down the other end, game over.” Even Brown admitted: “I thought it was stiff.” However, the decision to award Zorko a free was questioned. “It’s not much – that’s not a free kick, is it?” Ralph said of Weddle’s high contact. “Does he make the most of it?”

91b0d467-1e3f-4965-86e8-38429ea175c9.title: Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe narrowly avoided serious knee injury and surgery
91b0d467-1e3f-4965-86e8-38429ea175c9.incipit: Although the September international break came at a good time for Real Madrid, allowing the Merengue team some time to stop and reflect on their shortcomings in the first phase of the season, it has still...
91b0d467-1e3f-4965-86e8-38429ea175c9.body: Although the September international break came at a good time for Real Madrid, allowing the Merengue team some time to stop and reflect on their shortcomings in the first phase of the season, it has still brought its own set of bad news for Los Blancos. Only a few days after leaving the club to join his national team squad, Ibrahima Konate suffered a physical problem, which forced him to return to Real Madrid. Then, a few days later, Kylian Mbappe suffered an injury while playing for France against Turkiye, and alarm bells rang in the Spanish capital. Fortunately, detailed tests undertaken on the star forward after his return to the Merengue club showed that his injury was not too serious . He is suffering from a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of the knee, which is set to keep him out for around 10-12 days. However, Diario AS reports that the Frenchman was very close to suffering a very serious injury, one that could have kept him out of action for the entire season, and he avoided that only because he stopped playing right as he felt pain. In fact, Real Madrid initially believed that surgery might be necessary, but ultimately, it was confirmed that such a drastic measure was not necessary. Still, Los Blancos will take every possible caution with their star forward. Thus, even though he is expected to return to availability for the match against Villarreal on 10 October, Mourinho will play him only when there is no danger of long-term physical consequences. In this regard, the Real Madrid coach would be helped by the presence of other reliable options on the bench. One of these would be Carlos Espi, while the Portuguese coach can also field Jude Bellingham as a false 9, playing Arda Guler as an attacking midfielder behind him.

18de2d51-c6fe-4767-9e80-035df7f083eb.title: Kolisi says Australia clash a ‘big challenge’ for Boks
18de2d51-c6fe-4767-9e80-035df7f083eb.incipit: Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus and captain Siya Kolisi say South Africa are bracing themselves for a completely different challenge against the Wallabies in Perth next Sunday to that against the All Blacks in the RGR series.
18de2d51-c6fe-4767-9e80-035df7f083eb.body: Story audio is generated using AI Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus and captain Siya Kolisi say South Africa are bracing themselves for a completely different challenge against the Wallabies in Perth next Sunday to that which they faced in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Series against the All Blacks. Erasmus and Kolisi admitted that this match would test the team in various other ways. Erasmus also revealed that utility forward Pieter-Steph du Toit and centre Damian de Allende have been released from camp to spend time with their families after a demanding workload during RGR, with sufficient cover within the travelling squad for the match against the Wallabies. The teams will meet for the first time this year in a one-off Test at the Optus Stadium on Sunday, September 27, in a match that will be significant for both sides, with the 2027 Rugby World Cup set to be hosted in Australia, where the Boks will face Italy in their opening clash in Adelaide on Sunday, October 3. With much attention on the Springboks’ 3-1 RGR series win against the All Blacks, Erasmus said that competition was behind them now and emphasised that this clash was vital for the team before they embark on the second leg of the Nations Championship in November, where they will take on Italy, France and Ireland before the Finals Weekend. “This is a Test match against a country we’ve had a rivalry with since I can remember,” said Erasmus. “Since David Campese scored that beautiful try, Pieter Hendriks got the opening try against them in Cape Town at the 1995 Rugby World Cup, and since I played against players like George Gregan and Stephen Larkham when the Brumbies were one of the best teams in the world. “It’s not a tour we want to finish off casually. This is a great country, and the World Cup is being hosted here next year, so it’s massive to be able to play against the World Cup hosts in a big Test match.” Erasmus added: “They’ll be really fresh and they’ve won four out of five of their recent matches, while we come off a tough series against New Zealand. But RGR and this match have nothing to do with each other. This is a completely different challenge.” Kolisi agreed with Erasmus and said: “You always adjust for each team, but our core values are going to remain the same. Australia is completely different to New Zealand, so we’ll have to readjust certain things. It’s going to be a big challenge.” Commenting on how the players were feeling after the long journey from the US to Australia, where they are currently based in Terrigal north of Sydney, before making the trip to Perth next week Thursday, Kolisi said: “It’s been a long journey, but it was a great success in the USA, and being here in Australia now and preparing for this game is really important. “It’s a team we’ve had some tough battles against, but training has been going well this week and it’s good being here in Terrigal. We’ve also seen a lot of South Africans coming out here to support us, which is great.” The match next Sunday kicks off at 11.45am (SA time).

11c4ecae-e391-4ff7-bc9b-4db5999385ce.title: ‘Throw your medals in the bin,’ Roy Keane tells Manchester City players
11c4ecae-e391-4ff7-bc9b-4db5999385ce.incipit: Roy Keane said he would throw the ‘medals in the bin’ if he were a Manchester City player following Premier League confirmation that the club were guilty of all charges related to their financial rules
11c4ecae-e391-4ff7-bc9b-4db5999385ce.body: Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane said he would throw the “medals in the bin” if he were a Manchester City player following Premier League confirmation on Tuesday that the club were guilty of all charges related to their financial rules and boosted their income by more than £900m after arranging “sham ­contracts” with commercial partners. City, who continue to deny any wrongdoing, won eight trophies, including three Premier League titles between 2009 and 2018, the period under investigation. Keane said the achievements of City’s players had become redundant because of the “cheating” that took place during that time. “If I was a player, I’d be 100% sticking those medals in the bin. Of course you would, it’s cheating,” the ITV football pundit stated during the coverage of England’s match against the Czech Republic in the Nations League. “They won it on the pitch because cheating was going on.” And on the club he added: “They knew it would hurt a lot of people, but they’ve still done it.” Meanwhile, the former City defender Micah Richards says the damning verdict on the club has left him devastated and heartbroken. City were found to have engaged in an almost £1bn scheme to either inflate revenues or reduce costs through a series of “sham” arrangements in order to avoid breaching league and Uefa financial regulations. Speaking on The Rest is Football podcast, Richards said: “The reports were troubling. I saw the words which were used by the Premier League in sham contracts and I felt absolutely devastated. “I’ve been at that club since I was 14 years old, I would die for that club. I achieved my dream at Manchester City , but then to hear these reports, and not only me as an ex-player, but the fans, what they have to go through, absolutely devastating.” Richards described speaking to the fan he used to live with as a young player at the club, adding: “My digs man, he rang me and he was literally in tears and asking me about information, which I don’t know, I haven’t got the answers to tell him. “And that’s someone who’s supported the club for 60-odd years, and the uncertainty around it is just heartbreaking. To have a headline of this nature for a club that I love so much, it’s been difficult. If you listen to the reports, they are damning. I feel saddened, I feel angry, I feel a lit bit confused because, on the other side, you have City’s side of the story.”

e8eab597-e62c-4af3-8b18-6e53a32cc2ee.title: What tyres will the teams and drivers have for the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia?
e8eab597-e62c-4af3-8b18-6e53a32cc2ee.incipit: Following last weekend's dramatic race in Azerbaijan, the teams and drivers are heading to the Sepang International Circuit for the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix – and tyre suppliers Pirelli have confirmed...
e8eab597-e62c-4af3-8b18-6e53a32cc2ee.body: Following last weekend's dramatic race in Azerbaijan, the teams and drivers are heading to the Sepang International Circuit for the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix – and tyre suppliers Pirelli have confirmed the compounds that will be available. For F1's return to Malaysia after a nine-year absence, the C2, C3 and C4 have been selected as the hard, medium and soft compounds respectively. Drivers will get two sets of the hard tyre (marked white), three sets of the medium tyre (marked yellow), and eight sets of the soft tyre (marked red), as well as access to the green intermediate tyre and the blue full wets, should they be required. An extra set of softs is reserved for those who reach Q3 in Qualifying, while all drivers must use at least two different slick compounds during the race, providing the track is dry. "It is a track that generates medium energy levels through the tyres, placing it in a severity range comparable to Spa-Francorchamps and Shanghai," Pirelli’s weekend preview reads. "Ambient and track temperatures will be an important factor in tyre management, making thermal degradation one of the key variables throughout the weekend. "For the return to Kuala Lumpur, Pirelli has selected the C2, C3 and C4 compounds, designated respectively as hard, medium and soft. This choice is slightly more aggressive than the harder trio that would have represented a more conservative option given the characteristics of the circuit. The objective is to provide teams with a broader strategic range and create conditions in which the time difference between one-stop and two-stop strategies is reduced. "Sepang features a relatively abrasive surface, with a level of roughness comparable to Bahrain, while retaining its own distinctive characteristics. Grip levels are likely to be low on Friday but should improve progressively over the course of the weekend as the track evolves. One of the main challenges facing teams will be thermal management across both axles. "The circuit has undergone several changes in recent years. In 2023, the section between Turns 6 and 12 was resurfaced, with further work carried out in the area around Turn 9. However, the overall characteristics of the surface, as assessed by Pirelli engineers just a few weeks ago, remain very similar to those recorded in 2017. "More recently, from the beginning of September, additional surface levelling work was carried out to remove irregularities in the asphalt, alongside cleaning operations aimed at improving track conditions ahead of the World Championship event. "Teams will also have to contend with a lack of available data. Despite being a historic venue, no team possesses truly relevant references relating to the current generation of Formula 1 cars. "As a result, Friday practice sessions will be more important than usual, both for drivers, who will need to familiarise themselves with a circuit that many have only experienced in the simulator, and for teams, which must identify the correct car balance and assess tyre behaviour." f99e63e7-33e9-4c39-ae18-b1610f4c8f56.title: Japan Open suspended as tennis stars forced off and told to move court
f99e63e7-33e9-4c39-ae18-b1610f4c8f56.incipit: Play at the Japan Open was suspended for more than two hours (Image: ATP TOUR)Play at the Japan Open was suspended for more than two hours due to...
f99e63e7-33e9-4c39-ae18-b1610f4c8f56.body: Play at the Japan Open was suspended for more than two hours (Image: ATP TOUR) Play at the Japan Open was suspended for more than two hours due to heavy rain in Tokyo, leaving the players in limbo. The stoppage was declared midway through the first set of Jiri Lehecka's first-round match against Zizou Bergs, forcing them off the court. The rain continued to lash down for a couple of hours, forcing play at the ATP 500 event to remain stopped. Jean-Julien Roger and Theodore Winegar's doubles match against David Stevenson and Marcus Willis was also affected by the inclement weather. Some matches were eventually moved to other courts and rescheduled for later in the afternoon. Play eventually continued after the rain eased up and the outdoor courts were dried by members of staff. However, after only a brief period, another heavy shower caused additional delays. By that time, Lehecka had managed to win the first set against Bergs by six games to three. The second delay meant that play would not resume for another hour, with the rain showing little sign of slowing down. A couple of matches were played in full in spite of the weather, with Valentin Vacherot beating Alexander Blockx in straight sets and Alejandro Tabilo securing a comfortable win over Tommy Paul. It came after Lorenzo Musetti withdrew from the tournament at the eleventh hour, citing a broken finger. He was due to face British youngster Arthur Fery in the opening round. In a statement published on social media, the Italian said: "Unfortunately, I won't be able to play in Tokyo this year due to a small fracture in the ring finger of my right hand that I sustained during practice. "I'm very disappointed, especially because I couldn't wait to get back to playing in front of my Japanese fans and experience the wonderful atmosphere of Tokyo once again. "I will do everything I can in the next few days to recover and be ready to play in Shanghai. Thank you all for your support and for the many messages. I hope to see you very soon. See you soon, Japan." Musetti was replaced in the draw by lucky loser Jaime Faria, who has enjoyed a breakout season this year. If he beats Fery in the opening round, he will break into the top 60 of the ATP rankings. EXPRESS SPORT ON FB! Get all the best sports news and much more on our Facebook page .

d3ad771c-6349-4312-8271-5f3aac298aae.title: Trail Blazers Have Every Reason to Be Better Than Last Season
d3ad771c-6349-4312-8271-5f3aac298aae.incipit: With Ja Morant joining a healthy Damian Lillard and emerging star Deni Avdija, Portland boasts the elite offensive firepower...
d3ad771c-6349-4312-8271-5f3aac298aae.body: With Ja Morant joining a healthy Damian Lillard and emerging star Deni Avdija, Portland boasts the elite offensive firepower necessary to shatter expectations in a loaded West. The Portland Trail Blazers are coming off a 42-win season in which they made the playoffs as the seventh seed. That came just one year after winning 36 games and two years after winning only 21. There’s been clear, steady improvement from Portland over the past several seasons. Yet entering the 2026-27 campaign, most oddsmakers have the Blazers' win total sitting around 42.5. In other words, the expectation is essentially that Portland will be about as good as it was last season. Of course, it's never that simple. Strength of schedule matters, the rest of the Western Conference provides important context and injuries can change the trajectory of any season. But on paper, the Blazers have plenty of reason to believe they can be better than the team that won 42 games a year ago. For starters, Portland acquired Ja Morant, who immediately raises the offensive ceiling. There are legitimate questions about both his fit and health, but the Blazers added a player capable of consistently creating advantages off the dribble, putting pressure on the rim and generating opportunities for teammates. That's something last year's roster could have used. Then there's Damian Lillard, who essentially represents another addition despite technically being on the roster last season. After spending the year recovering, Lillard is finally healthy and ready to take the floor again. While Morant can bend defenses by attacking downhill, Lillard does it by stretching them well beyond the 3-point line. If both remain healthy, Portland suddenly has two very different types of offensive creators who can play off one another and make life easier for everyone else. Their presence also gives Portland tremendous backcourt depth, even with Shaedon Sharpe dealing with an injury. The Blazers can throw several different combinations on the floor depending on matchup and circumstance. And the reasons for optimism extend beyond the new-look backcourt. Donovan Clingan could emerge as one of the better young centers in the NBA this season. Deni Avdija has taken significant steps forward throughout his career and is coming off an All-Star season. Toumani Camara remains an important defensive piece, and Portland has enough established talent around its young core that continued internal improvement could make a meaningful difference. None of that guarantees the Blazers will make another major jump. Integrating Morant and Lillard will take time, and Portland is also entering its first season under head coach Micah Nori. In fact, it wouldn't be surprising if this is a team that gets noticeably better as the season progresses and everyone settles into their roles. But Portland doesn't need to become a 50-win contender overnight to clear a 42.5-win total. A jump into the 45-to-47-win range would be relatively modest considering where this team finished last season and the talent it added. There's real reason to believe last year's 42-win season wasn't Portland's ceiling. It may simply have been another step in a climb that isn't finished yet. 7a604efb-5d60-42aa-a2df-38fc67e7adf8.title: Wang and Higa Set Blistering Early Pace
7a604efb-5d60-42aa-a2df-38fc67e7adf8.incipit: Aichi, Japan: Chinese Taipei’s Wang Wei-hsuan produced a faultless performance to earn a share of the opening round lead with home favourite Kazuki Higa as golf joined the party at the 20th Asian Games.
7a604efb-5d60-42aa-a2df-38fc67e7adf8.body: Aichi, Japan: Chinese Taipei’s Wang Wei-hsuan produced a faultless performance to earn a share of the opening round lead with home favourite Kazuki Higa as golf joined the party at the 20th Asian Games. Published September 30, 2026 Kasugai, Aichi, Japan: Chinese Taipei’s Wang Wei-hsuan produced a faultless performance to earn a share of the opening round lead with home favourite Kazuki Higa as golf joined the party at the 20th Asian Games. Aided by an eagle-two at the fifth hole, Wang returned a bogey-free five-under-par 65 at the Kasugai Country Club’s East Course in Aichi Prefecture. Higa, last year’s Asian Tour Order of Merit champion, was six-under through 16 but dropped his only stroke of the day at the 506-yard, par-four 17th, statistically the most difficult hole on the course. Heading into Thursday’s second round, Wang and Higa hold a one-stroke lead from Indian Saptak Talwar , Korean Mun Do-yeob , China’s Sampson Zheng Yunhe and Japan’s Keita Nakajima . A further stroke back in joint seventh are China’s Ding Wenyi and Korean Tom Kim Joo-hyung , the highest-rated player in the 66-strong men’s field at 32nd in the Official World Golf Ranking. Hong Kong China’s Taichi Kho began his quest for back-to-back individual gold medals with a one-under 69. The highlight of his round came at the par-three seventh where he holed his seven-iron tee shot from 183 yards. In the team event in which the best two daily scores in each three-man team are counted, Japan leads the way on nine-under 131, courtesy of Higa’s 65 and Nakajima’s 66. Two strokes back in joint second are Korea and China with Chinese Taipei fourth on 136. Wang, who celebrated his 27th birthday last Sunday, lived upto his reputation as one of golf’s longest hitters, averaging 320 yards off the tee. Following a perfect drive at the 441-yard fifth, he holed out with a 52-degree wedge from 113 yards. “I hit it pretty good. I didn’t see it go in because the green is elevated, but my wife and dad were at the green cheering,” said Wang, who is representing Chinese Taipei for the third time at the Asian Games. “The first two times, I was a little bit nervous. But this time, I’m just playing with freedom, like normal. I’m pretty excited for this week,” he added. Also feeling excited is Higa, especially at the prospect of challenging for the team gold with Nakajima and amateur Taishi Moto , the third member of the Japanese team. “It’s a great start for us. It’s up to the two professional players – me and Keita – to lead, so that Taishi can play freely. He struggled today (74) but we have three more days, so he can try whatever he wants to do. We back him,” said Higa, who is encouraging Japanese fans to support their medal bid. “There were many fans cheering us. I want to see more of them come out this week to cheer for Team Japan.” Kazuki Higa helped Japan to the top of the leaderboard in the team event. Picture by Asian Tour. b0b29f85-efbf-4eac-a5e5-8889bfb51eed.title: Inter's Half-Time 'Medicine': Comeback King Lautaro Declares 'First Half to Forget'
b0b29f85-efbf-4eac-a5e5-8889bfb51eed.incipit: The Nerazzurri captain was the star of the second half, scoring a brace to secure a draw against Roma. 'It's clear we need to review how we start; always chasing is difficult,' he admitted.
b0b29f85-efbf-4eac-a5e5-8889bfb51eed.body: The Nerazzurri captain was the protagonist in the second half, scoring a brace that secured the draw against Roma: "It's clear we need to review how we start; always chasing is difficult." Scegli Gazzetta come fonte preferita su Google It all seems to revolve around two distinct 15-minute periods. There's the first, the opening quarter of the match, where Inter sometimes appear unable to get going. Distracted, complacent, even superficial, they concede unthinkable goals in a way they wouldn't in any other period of play. It's strange, something to investigate (and Chivu, along with his staff, is already working on this issue), but it's a recurring pattern. Then there's the other 15-minute period to pay attention to: the one between one half and the other. It's no secret that this Inter side has the ability to regenerate themselves precisely at half-time. This tendency is a legacy from last season. But confidence grows when Lautaro makes the difference, becoming a key factor in their comebacks. Comeback King — Yesterday's two goals, which took his tally to five in the last five clashes against the Giallorossi, averted defeat, while the other two he scored this season against Napoli had directly secured victory for Inter. Total: four. Both the league goals so far, and, more importantly, the points delivered to his team. So, it's fair to say that almost a third of Inter's 13 points in the table today belong to the Argentine. Lautaro embodies Chivu's philosophy when his coach says: "We must act, not react." When "El Toro" performs, the comeback is on. They just need to get the right balls to him, something Inter struggled greatly with in the first half yesterday. But Dybala, who knows his compatriot and Inter well, had made an unmistakable gesture to his teammates after Koné's first goal. Palms down, as if to say: "Calm down." It's impossible to celebrate victory too early against this team, who may have conceded seven goals in their last three league matches and gone two goals down in those same outings, but they've always managed to bounce back when they've hit rock bottom. And the face of the comeback is once again Lautaro's, angular and furious, but ultimately joyful. Inter's Saviour — His half-smile after the match was an inevitable reaction, and he himself immediately and unequivocally explained why: "We had a first half to forget. We didn't turn up, and our attitude wasn't right." His words were sharp. He continued: "In the second half, however, we immediately changed our mentality. When you play these matches," Lautaro went on, "if you waste a half, it becomes difficult: we couldn't get the three points, we're left with one, which is still excellent considering what Roma are doing." But why these slow starts? "It's a matter of attitude and preparing for matches correctly: we do it, but it's clear we need to review how we start. Always chasing is difficult." Another headline of the evening, however, came from the other half of "ThuLa": "Lauti saved us again..." was Thuram's honest summary. 749061f6-7129-4d7d-b719-c3a366303dde.incipit: The winner of the 2026 men's Stawell Gift has been suspended from competition for 12 months after failing a drug test. Sports Integrity Australia...
749061f6-7129-4d7d-b719-c3a366303dde.body: The winner of the 2026 men's Stawell Gift has been suspended from competition for 12 months after failing a drug test. Sports Integrity Australia confirmed Olufemi "Femi" Komolafe had recorded a positive drug test for ADHD medication. Stawell Gift organisers did not confirm whether he will be required to return his winnings from the race. This year's Stawell Gift men's winner, Olufemi "Femi" Komolafe, has been suspended for 12 months after testing positive for ADHD medication. The 21-year-old set a new personal best to claim his first major title in April this year, and also claimed the $40,000 prize for placing first in the annual 120-metre handicapped sprint. Komolafe was given a 5-metre handicap in this year's race, starting behind all but one of his opponents in the final. But Sports Integrity Australia has handed down a 12-month ban, confirming Komolafe had tested positive for the banned medication. ADHD medications are banned in sport for their potential performance-enhancing effects, with athletes only able to use them if they have a medical diagnosis and it is part of treatment. Stawell Gift organisers have not confirmed whether Komolafe will be asked to return his winnings or whether he will be stripped of his title. The ban comes as Sports Integrity Australia expresses concerns over the prevalence of athletes using ADHD medications without a formal diagnosis. In July, its chief executive, Sarah Benson, said she was seeing a "significant number" of inadvertent doping violations from high-level Australian athletes using ADHD medication. Dr Benson said the consequences are severe for athletes found breaching the rules. "Since these medications could be abused by athletes for performance improvement reasons, the tough reality is that they are banned under the World Anti-Doping Code if the athlete does not have a formal diagnosis," Dr Benson said. "Under the Code, this is true even if they establish their diagnosis after the positive test, and they face a ban of one to four years."
